reason: Driven at 1440x960 and 390x844: type 3 October 2026, press Set the day, harvest the answered frame. The geometry is as described (count 148px/96px, .b-emptyBody 17px at y512, the button at y591, #b-empty-hint at y642 - 130px top-to-top), but the characterisation and the fix both fail. (1) Factually wrong on the core claim. The three items are not the same instruction. "Nothing sits between today and the day yet" describes state; "Everything you add is measured from it" states the page's law; "The day is set." confirms the transaction that just completed. Only "Moments come next" plus the button label point forward, and there is exactly ONE control on the frame, offered once. The defect-library class invoked - "an empty surface offers exactly one instruction, once - not four templated 'Nothing here' lines" (lessons.md:74-76) - targets competing boilerplate across empty regions, and this frame satisfies it. The hint is also 13px, not the 15px asserted. (2) The fix breaks two passing gate assertions. interaction-check.mjs:1499 asserts the accepted answer at #b-empty-hint begins "The day is set" 150ms after the press, and :699 asserts /day is set/i at 250ms. "Clear #b-empty-hint after the surface re-renders" fails both. That sentence is not incidental copy: round 3 built a deliberate four-sentence answer vocabulary for this field (three refusals plus one acceptance) and the gate locks it; deleting the acceptance leaves the product able to refuse three ways and unable to say yes. (3) The fix's accessibility premise is wrong, which is the part that makes it a regression rather than a wash. render-b.js:1244 mutates the OLD hint to "The day is set. Moments come next.", then line 1264 replaceChild's the whole .b-empty away in the same synchronous task. A live region mutated and detached inside one task is routinely dropped by NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver, and the surviving carrier - the new #b-empty-hint inserted with its text already present - is itself unreliably announced, since screen readers announce changes to live regions already in the tree, not content present at insertion. So the sentence's only guaranteed accessibility today is that it is persistent, readable text in the accessibility tree. Clearing it turns "announced once" into a race the fix assumes it wins, on the first screen of the product, for the audience the brief names. (4) Part A removes the only sentence on this frame that teaches the page's law to a first-timer, at the exact moment the law stops being abstract ("it" was an unknown day one screen ago; here it is 79 and Saturday 3 October 2026). Restating a rule when it becomes concrete is a teaching move; the finding offers no argument for why the echo costs more than a first-timer not learning the rule, against a north star that ranks Utility for someone who has never used a tool like this. The finding does not revert round 6 - the Add a moment button stays wired - but round 6's own verdict leaned on "the frame has just said Moments come next and focused the control" as the promise that button now keeps.
sharpenedFix: There is one real kernel worth keeping: "Everything on this page is measured from it" (render-b.js:1196) and "Everything you add is measured from it" (render-b.js:1259) are near-identical constructions one screen apart, so the echo reads as a copy accident rather than a deliberate return. Fix that by rewording the second, not by deleting a sentence and not by clearing a role="status" line: keep .b-emptyBody at two sentences but let the second land on the new concrete anchor - e.g. "Nothing sits between today and the day yet. Every moment you add will sit somewhere in that gap." That kills the verbatim repeat, keeps the law taught where it first becomes real, leaves #b-empty-hint and the four-sentence answer vocabulary intact, and breaks no gate assertion. If the panel still wants the hint quieter after the transaction, the safe move is to demote it visually while leaving it in the accessibility tree, never to empty it.
